# D8_TRIGDEBUG_L6547965c: swing_pct_8 bars + trig_tape_unfinished unf_fade (m 6, cp 0.0), NY AM session of trading date 20261110 plus the 300 bars before it (W-D8SPEC, relay order 0400Z)

Documentation only. Series: ONE continuous series of all bars of row `swing_pct_8` (all sessions, 2023-04 to 2026-11-13, 200,662 bars, stored engine bars = the BASE set: price-path bars are unaffected by the print rule, same open/high/low/close and extreme times; the book runs on these bars). Rows below: bar index 198815 to 199312; the NY AM bars of 20261110 are sess 3 and td 20261110 (idx 199115 to 199312, 198 bars; 11 events). **Checks:** (1) my footprint recompute from the tape (every print with exchange time in the bar window) equals the stored feature columns f_hi_bid, f_hi_ask, f_lo_bid, f_lo_ask on all 498 rows shown (0 differences); (2) my event rule applied to the stored features equals the module's `signal_fn` on the whole series except bar 0 of the series (18,305 module signals, 18,304 mine; the one difference is the very first bar, an edge artefact); (3) the book's engine entry/exit settings are plain 60/60 (stop 60, target 60 points), flat at session end (12:00 ET = 17:00 UTC), 120 s exit cap.

## 1. The bar: swing_pct_8 (code `th_bars/kernels.py k_dchg`; rule D8_BAR_DEFS.md section 3.10)
- Zig-zag leg bars: a bar = the leg from the previous extreme to the new extreme, **confirmed** when price retraces theta ticks from the extreme. **theta = max(2, round(8 x price_in_ticks / 10000))** recomputed at every print from that print's price: 89 ticks (about 22.25 points) at the start of the NY AM session and 88 ticks at its end on 20261110 (column `theta ticks` is theta at the bar's close price). Bar O = previous extreme, C = the new extreme (H or L the same), **t0 = the confirming print of the previous leg (start of this leg's window), t1 = the time of the extreme print (first print at the extreme price), known time = the confirming print** (the bar is known theta ticks after the extreme was made). State resets at session boundaries; an unfinished leg at the session end is dropped.

## 2. What tape data the trigger reads (code: `triggers_c/defs.py _unf`, `featc.py _bar_kernel`)
- For each bar it takes **every trade print (price, size, aggressor side) whose exchange timestamp lies in [t0, t1] inclusive** (all prints from the previous leg's confirming print up to and including all prints that share the extreme print's timestamp; searchsorted left on t0, right on t1 over the sorted exchange timestamps). From these prints it builds a per-price footprint: for each price row (one tick) the **ask volume** (sum of sizes of BUY-aggressor prints) and the **bid volume** (sum of sizes of SELL-aggressor prints); a print with unknown side would be split half/half (none occur with the quote rule). Only the four numbers at the two extreme rows are used: **f_hi_bid / f_hi_ask** = sell-/buy-aggressor volume at the HIGHEST price traded in the window, **f_lo_bid / f_lo_ask** = the same at the LOWEST price. The window's high/low rows come from these prints (not from the bar's o/h/l/c columns; they agree for a leg bar). If the window spans more than 400 ticks (range rows > 400) the features are NaN and no signal is possible.
- **Unfinished high** = f_hi_bid == 0 (no sell-aggressor volume at the high row) AND f_hi_ask >= m = 6 contracts. **Unfinished low** = f_lo_ask == 0 AND f_lo_bid >= 6. cp = 0.0 means no close-position gate. **unf_fade:** SHORT at an unfinished high and LONG at an unfinished low (a bar with both is dropped); events are edges (condition true now and false on the previous bar), part = 1 bars and the warm-up give none. Event time = floor(known time to whole seconds) + 2 s.
- **Can NT8 compute it from last/bid/ask ticks alone? Yes in principle, with three cautions.** (a) It needs only the tick stream (price, size, and a buy/sell classification per tick: last >= ask = buy aggressor, last <= bid = sell aggressor, which is exactly the D8 side rule; the engine flag agrees with it except on a few contracts per session (opening prints and ties)), keeping a volume-by-price table (bid volume and ask volume per tick price) for the current leg window. (b) The test is brutally sensitive: ONE contract of sell-aggressor volume at the high row kills an unfinished-high signal, so a single mis-classified tick or a missing tick at the extreme row changes the event; the CQG feed is the same contract-by-contract stream (D8_FEED_CHECK.md section 7: 0 side mismatches) so this is exact on matching data. (c) The window boundaries use exchange timestamps: the window starts at the previous leg's confirming print and ends at the time of the extreme; in the CQG feed timestamps are jittered (p99 +43 ms Asia, +592 ms NY AM), so prints within that jitter of t0 or t1 can fall on the other side of the window; implement the window by tick ORDER (from the confirming tick up to the last tick at the extreme price's first occurrence plus all ticks sharing its timestamp) rather than by wall-clock to avoid it. No order book is needed.

## 4. History NT8 must carry (plain paragraph)
The bar state (swing legs) restarts at every session boundary, so the swing bars of the NY AM session need only the session's own ticks from 09:30 ET (the first leg is decided after theta ticks of movement), and the footprint of each bar needs only the ticks since the previous leg's confirming tick, so NO long history is required beyond the session. Per-session start-up: the first bar of the session is emitted at the first confirmed reversal; the first leg's window starts at the session's first print. The only history-dependent element of the book is the series edge rule (no event on the very first bar of the series).
